answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting. Each identity gets a cipher-keyed hash of its interaction timing, order, and counterparty mix; the hash must stay within a similarity band across epochs or the identity is frozen. Attackers running many clones on one operator cannot keep independent fingerprints synchronized, since a single orchestration pattern repeats like a vine across accounts and gets flagged. Maintaining distinct, plausible behaviour per clone costs continuous manual tuning and delays, while the tundra of dormant periods still requires seeded activity to survive scoring.
